notes.text: Claim that the compiler emits no warning for calling a non-readonly method on a readonly struct field: true for the C# compiler itself; some IDE analyzers may flag it. The field initializer avoids CS0649.

bugLineSets accepts either line 15 (readonly field declaration) or line 17 (the Increment call). Check line numbers: line 15 is `private readonly Counter _counter = new Counter();`, line 17 is `public void Track() => _counter.Increment();`.
Assumed that the readonly keyword page and/or the struct page on Microsoft Learn describe the defensive-copy behaviour for readonly fields of mutable structs; verify the excerpts support it.

Claim that a `readonly struct` makes `Value++` in Increment fail to compile: in a readonly struct all instance fields must be readonly and `this` is readonly in members, so the assignment is rejected. No specific error code is stated.
